_meta.purpose: How lenses/nutrition.py reads a nutrition table the vision model transcribed (D-133): which printed row is which nutrient, its unit, and FSSAI's own figures for checking the table's arithmetic. The model copies the table; these rules interpret it (D-004).

source.title: FSS (Labelling and Display) Regulations 2020, 5(3), compendium version I (23.09.2021)

_meta.how_to_use: A printed row label is lower-cased, its leading '-' and 'of which' dropped, and matched against 'names' in the order below, whole words: the first row that matches wins, so the more specific names come first (added sugars before sugars, saturated fat before fat). 'ignore' rows are read and set aside.

rda_basis._note: 5(3)(b): per serve % contribution to RDA is calculated on 2000 kcal energy, 67 g total fat, 22 g saturated fat, 2 g trans fat, 50 g added sugar and 2000 mg sodium (5 g salt) for an average adult per day. A printed % RDA that doesn't fit the per 100 figure and the serving size means a number was read into the wrong row, or the serving size was misread.

energy_factors._note: 5(3)(e)(i): kcal per gram, for working out what share of a food's energy comes from its fat.
